item.title: Shift at Midnight: Calendar Killer, Explained
item.description:
Not every mystery in Shift at Midnight has a clear answer. Some, like Norbert the Gnome, eventually reveal themselves, but others can leave players scratching their heads.

One of the biggest is the Calendar Killer. The game brings it up through a broadcast message. But after that, players expect something to happen and are left wondering if they missed an encounter. Here's everything we know about the Calendar Killer in Shift at Midnight.

Shift at Midnight: How Many Players Can Play?

Want to play Shift at Midnight with a bigger group? Here's the official player limit and how to increase it with mods!

By Umama Ali

Who is the Calendar Killer in Shift at Midnight?

At the end of your seventh shift , you will see a broadcast about the Calendar Killer:

The killer known as the Calendar Killer is scheduled to be active tomorrow, following their pattern of killing 8 people on the 8th of every month since July. Stay safe. Stay inside. Stay alert.

​

The message makes it sound like you're about to come face to face with the Calendar Killer during your next shift. Naturally, that's what I expected too, but the eighth shift plays out like normal with no sign of the killer . I also watched several playthroughs and speedruns, and the same thing happened there.

Once the shift ends, the game shows you another broadcast message:

Despite matching up with their recurring killing patterns, it seems that the Calendar Killer did not strike for the first time in six months. Has the Calendar Killer lost their nerve?

​

Does the Calendar Killer Exist in Shift at Midnight?

​Right now, there’s no clear answer. One theory that caught my attention is that your character is actually the Calendar Killer. The biggest piece of evidence is that the Calendar Killer never visits your shop on the eighth shift. Instead, exactly eight customers visit the store that night. This matches the broadcast that says the killer claims eight victims on the eighth day of the month.

Having said that, I wasn't able to verify the theory myself. I didn't kill all eight customers during that shift, so I can't say whether doing so changes anything or triggers a secret event.

Curious for more answers about the Calendar Killer and other Shift at Midnight mysteries? Subscribing to the newsletter offers in-depth theories, playthrough findings, and community-sourced reproduction attempts to help you explore this mystery and similar indie game secrets.
By subscribing, you agree to receive newsletter and marketing emails, and accept our Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. You can unsubscribe anytime.

Of course, there's another possibility. The Calendar Killer might not be meant to appear at all. Shift at Midnight already has a few mysteries that never lead anywhere. The Missing Dog Guillermo is a good example. The game tells you about it, but you never actually find it. The Calendar Killer could be the same kind of mystery.

item.title: BREAKING: EA's $55 Billion Sale is Now Finalized
item.description:
The sale of Electronic Arts for $55 billion USD has officially been completed as of August 4. The previously public company will be removed from the stock market, as EA will now be fully private.

EA was originally established back in 1982, and has been a publicly-traded company since 1989. Back in 2025, EA announced that it would be sold, making it just one of the many game industry companies experiencing major shake-ups in recent times.

Dragon Age Producer Addresses Possibility of Remasters

Dragon Age's series producer discusses the possibility of remasters for the early games in the series, and reveals a significant problem.

By Sarah Fields

EA Acquired for $55 Billion

It was previously revealed that the EA acquisition deal was expected to close on August 4, and that has turned out to be accurate, as EA has now officially gone private. Per a press release, the acquisition of EA by PIF, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners, which are collectively being referred to as The Consortium, has been completed. The $55 billion deal is the biggest leveraged buyout ever, which has seen $20 billion added to EA's overall debt. With the company's removal from the stock market, stockholders will be granted $210 for every piece of EA common stock that they owned when the deal was completed. Multiple parties involved in the acquisition have shared statements praising EA, and sharing plans to focus on sustained growth, innovation, and in AI to "enhance game development and player experience."

Although the purchase has now been completed, it hasn't been a very smooth path to get to that point. Concerns have been raised by gamers, with some expressing worries that EA's properties would experience changes under the new ownership. This has been of particular concern to The Sims 4 's community, as the game has often been celebrated for its inclusive themes. In this deal, the majority owner of Electronic Arts will be the Public Investment Fund of Saudia Arabia, and gamers have been worried that its ownership could mean changes to existing game franchises. However, EA has tried to assuage those concerns leading up to the closure of this deal.

Gamers haven't been the only pushback regarding this deal, as it faced some issues from lawmakers, as well. US Democrats urged the Federal Trade Commission Chair to review the acquisition, and US Representative Maxwell Frost held a livestream with former EA content creator Lilsimsie in opposition to the acquisition. An opposition protest was also held outside EA headquarters. However, those efforts ultimately turned out to be largely fruitless, as the deal has now closed.

As noted, this is far from the only major change transpiring in the game industry in recent times. In addition to numerous developer layoffs and entire closures of studios, Xbox has been making waves by undergoing major restructuring, which led to 1,600 roles being eliminated earlier in 2026. However, 3,200 jobs in total are expected to be cut at Xbox by the end of fiscal year 2027. Sony has been no stranger to layoffs either, with 60% of the studios owned by Sony experiencing layoffs or being closed entirely since 2019. For now, it remains to be seen if the industry can find stability, or if it will continue to see massive changes like these continue in the years to come.

item.title: 5 Near-Perfect Single-Player FPS Games Nobody Played
item.description:
Ever since Wolfenstein and Doom , FPS games have refused to stop coming out. Even as AAA publishers moved away from non-franchise shooters in the late 2010s, indie devs stepped up to right that wrong, producing a new golden era. With competition so fierce, fantastic FPS games frequently slip through the cracks while everyone's attention lies elsewhere (on COD or Apex Legends ).

As the gaming industry moves at a blistering pace, convincing anybody to try out a forgotten shooter from 2004 is a tough task, but that won't stop us from spotlighting these games. If you feel a bit disenchanted with the current FPS scene, a trip to the past, when publishers were willing to take risks and get weird with their games, might be in order.

I'm focusing on great games that flopped at launch and haven't really become well-known cult classics (so, no Bulletstorm ). While I would recommend all these games to anybody who enjoys old-school shooters, I'm not taking into account how well they have aged.

Clive Barker’s Undying Should Be Horror-FPS Royalty

Much Better Than The Other Clive Barker Horror-FPS Game

  • A 2001 PC FPS horror game that wasn't marketed particularly well by EA Games.
  • Undying is still accessible through GOG.

While Jericho was a disappointment, Clive Barker's name isn't associated solely with lackluster shooters, even if you have to push past some unsurprising early-2000s jank. Undying absolutely oozes Lovecraftian gothic horror , blending fun dual-wielding mechanics with a delightfully creepy premise that involves curses, vengeful undead beings, and occult goodness.

With Barker contributing to the lore and characters, Undying showcases his signature style, and EA Los Angeles did a pretty good job of creating a solid shooter-horror hybrid around the author's concepts. The story revolves around siblings who unleashed occult magic and became cursed to die gruesomely, and you portray a WWI vet tasked with tracking and putting them down. Just silly B-Movie horror goodness.

Although a bit rough around the edges, Undying 's combat still shines due to its innovative implementation of dual-wielding , with one hand holding weapons and the other dedicated to spells or gestures. Besides combat, spells like the Scrye played a significant role in exploration, allowing you to see things that you would otherwise miss.

8 Great FPS Games You Cannot Buy Anymore

These FPS games are fantastic, but sadly, they were delisted and evaporated from the digital store shelves.

6
By Mark Sammut

Kingpin: Life of Crime Was Blackballed Into Video Game Jail

An Ambitious Forward-Thinking FPS Game That Is Also Delightfully Gritty

  • A gritty 1999 FPS that fell prey to media backlash and wasn't even available in certain retail chains.
  • Kingpin: Life of Crime is still available on Steam.

Although you never know how a gritty shooter from a relatively unknown developer will perform, Kingpin: Life of Crime would have fared much better if it hadn't been released a few months after the Columbine High School massacre.

Unsurprisingly, the media targeted the title as part of its scapegoating campaign against video game violence, greatly limiting its reach and dooming it to instant obscurity. Kingpin deserves to be remembered as one of the Quake II engine's crowning achievements , and as a forward-thinking project that explored mechanics that would eventually become popular in the FPS genre.

Hitboxes tied to specific body parts let players shoot enemies in the leg or arm to impact their abilities, a concept that is fairly ordinary nowadays. Although level-based, Kingpin actually gives NPCs personality and lets you adapt your approach when interacting with them, and it even features weapon modification through pawn shops during a time when that was not remotely commonplace. The Cypress Hill soundtrack matched the grimy urban environment splendidly, creating a game that felt different from everything else at the time of its release.

Tron 2.0 Continued The Franchise's Tradition By Being A High-Quality Flop

This Disney FPS Game Should Be Played By Everyone

  • What a surprise; a Tron property flopped.
  • Tron 2.0 is still available on Steam. Disney's recent history of suddenly delisting games puts Tron 2.0 's future in doubt. Keep that in mind if you're interested in picking this one up.

The developer responsible for Blood , The Operative: No One Lives Forever , F.E.A.R. , and Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor created a Tron FPS game. Yes, I was also caught off-guard by this tidbit, but Monolith Productions not only created Tron 2.0 ​​​​, but it also brought its A-game.

Serving as a sequel to the original movie, Tron 2.0 goes out of its way to faithfully recreate the world and aesthetic of its cinematic predecessor , all the while acting as a fantastic standalone shooter for anybody who doesn't want to do any homework. Monolith designed the mechanics around the setting, creating perfect harmony between the story, environments, and combat. For instance, your inventory is represented through RAM slots, and weapons are subroutines that can have corrupted code.

Despite the Disney association, Tron 2.0 is a hardcore shooter by a master of the genre , one packed with tech jargon and light RPG mechanics. Reviews were very positive, but not all that many folks paid attention to a licensed game in an obscure franchise published by Mickey Mouse.

Breakdown Is Unlike Any Other 2004 FPS Game

Honestly, It Is Unlike Any FPS Game, Period

  • A 2004 Namco game that was an Xbox exclusive. Limited NA marketing doomed this experimental genre-combo before it ever had a chance.
  • Backward compatible with Xbox 360, One, and Series X/S.

Before Cyberpunk 2077 or even Mirror's Edge , Breakdown stepped up to revolutionize first-person immersion , only to be promptly ignored by the entire world. Throughout the campaign, the game never moves away from the protagonist's first-person perspective and takes steps to emphasize realistic interactions, despite the story and setting being over-the-top sci-fi awesomeness.

Breakdown took a shocking number of risks for both the era and developer, as Namco wasn't known for first-person games except for arcade light-gun shooters and some obscure PS1 titles from the early '90s. The locked POV would become relatively commonplace towards the end of the 2000s, but most subsequent games didn't take things as far as Breakdown in recreating realistic human movement.

Combat blends melee and firearms, with the former being far more useful and developed. Breakdown functions as a first-person brawler with gunplay rather than an FPS with punches , and the player's abilities reach absurd heights by the end of the campaign. You will be unleashing shockwaves and energy shields before you know it.

10 Classic FPS Games You Must Play In 2026

These fantastic old-school first-person shooters are readily available on Steam and GOG, but they might not always be around.

1
By Mark Sammut

Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth Was Left To Die On Xbox

Still One Of The Best Lovecraftian Horror Games (And A Pretty Good FPS Game, Too)

  • 6 years of development hell led to a 2005 Xbox-only release, just a month before the Xbox 360's debut.
  • Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth is available on Steam, but the PC port is notoriously broken and buggy. The PC version is about as far removed from "near-perfect" as a game gets. The Xbox version is way more stable, although not free of bugs.

Resulting in Headfirst Productions' bankruptcy, Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth walked through hell to reach its finishing line, only to die a quick and silent death on the original Xbox. While preserved on PC, that port launched as a mess and has only become worse with each new operating system, making it near-impossible to recommend unless somebody is prepared to fix it themselves.

Sadly, way too many people will never get to experience one of the best Lovecraftian games, along with one of the better horror-FPS releases of the 2000s. Beating Dead Space to the punch by a couple of years, Dark Corners of the Earth adopted a HUD-less design that forces players to physically complete "simple" tasks like physically checking their remaining bullets or using realistic tools to heal injuries. Although not the first to go down this route, the game incorporated a Sanity system that could trigger hallucinations or panic attacks.

item.title: Lord of the Rings: The Wolves of Mordor Officially Announced
item.description:
Sauron's defeat may have ended The Lord of the Rings , but Middle-earth has never run out of stories to tell, with one coming this fall specifically focused on the werewolves of Middle-earth. Long before he forged the One Ring and ruled from Barad-dur, Sauron carried another title: the Lord of Werewolves. That forgotten piece of Tolkien lore (mostly explored in The Silmarillion rather than The Lord of the Rings itself) is finally stepping into the spotlight with a brand-new adventure set deep inside Mordor.

Mordor itself has always been more than ash, lava, and the Eye of Sauron. Beyond the familiar plains of Gorgoroth are regions rarely explored across Lord of the Rings games, books, or films, with their own history, civilizations, and creatures that never reached the front lines of the War of the Ring. That's exactly where Standing Stone Games is taking fans of Lord of the Rings next, swapping familiar battlefields for unexplored corners of the Dark Land filled with experiments, buried societies, and werewolves created during Sauron's rise to power.

5 Best Lord of the Rings Characters Cut From the Movies (& Why)

Some of the best characters from Tolkien's books never made it to the LotR movies, & the reasons behind these cuts help explain how the films work.

By Ashley Turner

The Lord of Wolves, the Draugardh, and New Regions of Mordor, Oh My

That's the foundation for The Lord of the Rings Online: The Wolves of Mordor , the MMO's next expansion launching this fall. As first reported in MMORPG.com's exclusive on Wolves of Mordor, the update explores three new regions of Mordor: Heledhris, Parth Rhavas, and Nan Ogol. It'll also focus on Sauron's time as the Lord of Wolves, at least some of it, while introducing the Draugardh, a society of intelligent werewolves inspired by Tolkien's writings.

LOTRO players will unlock new skills, tactical abilities, enhancements, and passive bonuses instead of simply grinding for more levels, with Standing Stone Games saying the system is designed to carry forward into future expansions. Alongside it comes the Neighbor system, letting players build friendships with NPC companions through housing, gifts, quests, and daily interactions, which is certainly an exciting addition for LOTRO .

Players will also encounter three distinct werewolf factions, surviving Easterlings, Woses, Gondorian scouts, Elves, and Dunedain while exploring volcanic mountain ranges and Nan Ogol, a prehistoric jungle filled with creatures and laboratories where LOTR 's Sauron once conducted terrifying experiments. New three-player and six-player instances, plus a raid planned before the end of the year, round out the brand-new LOTRO expansion's PvE offerings.

item.title: Pokemon Pokopia Free Update Finally Fixes Its Biggest Problem
item.description:
Pokemon Pokopia 's paid Bubbly Basin DLC is getting all the attention, as perhaps it should, but the accompanying free update for all players is making a major fix to ease some of the rough edges in-game. Of course, the new town, the new content, and the new Pokemon coming to Pokopia with Bubbly Basin are a big deal, but it shouldn't overshadow the best new item coming as part of the free update.

To be perfectly clear, Pokemon Pokopia 's Bubbly Basin DLC releases at 9 PM PT on August 4, 12 AM ET on August 5, and it brings with it a ton of new content: the Dive exploration mechanic, 3D underwater building mechanics, a new biome in an underwater town, and much more. That's one thing. Alongside it is the release of a free content update, a completely second and separate thing. Every feature in Bubbly Basin is paid, but the free content update goes live for all Pokemon Pokopia players at the same time.

All Pokopia DLC Leaks Online

Ahead of any official announcement, a full list of new regions planned for Pokemon Pokopia DLC leaks online, revealing major expansions.

By Joshua Duckworth

Pokopia Free Update Adds Major QoL Storage Feature

Pokemon Pokopia 's free content update is adding a new storage chest to the game, a free update item, that fixes its biggest crafting issue. As many Pokopia players know, this beloved Pokemon life sim requires tons of items and crafting all across its map, and this can result in key crafting items being left in separate chests in completely different Pokopia biomes. Then players must undergo a Hero's Journey to find said items, either in which chest they left it or again in the world, to complete whatever task lies before them. That's a thing of the past, as reported by Famitsu.

New Questions Added!

GameRant Quiz

—

QUESTION 1/1

Results

0

—

More Games

According to Famitsu, the free update introduces a new "sharing device" storage option (likely in the form of a new chest) that can access shared items between them. In short, one of these chests can be placed in every base and biome, and kept in inventory to have quick, instant access to tons of items. Famitsu's testing may not be exhaustive, but it reports that each device has a storage of 20 and that it was able to deploy 20 of them for a total of 140 storage slots in Pokopia . This, no doubt, made accessing various items much, much easier.

Pokemon Pokopia Free Update Finally Fixes Its Biggest Problem
New Pokemon Release Officially Confirmed for August 5
Pokemon Pokopia Has 31 Confirmed New Pokemon Coming in Bubbly Basin
First Look at New Pokemon Pokopia Dress-Up Feature

Plus, it can be crafted via the various recipes in Pokopia , letting players make more (presumably to a certain point). That makes crafting these items easier. It's worth noting that they can also be placed on Pokopia' s Cloud Islands, but they can only access items within that Cloud Island. When deployed properly, it seems that these storage options will bring the aforementioned Hero's Journey to an end.

Find the odd one out before the timer hits zero.

Bubbly Basin and this free content update is the first major post-launch release for Pokopia , obviously not counting routine updates and events, and it's clear that the developers are not holding back. Not to put the Ponyta before the Sharpedo, but that bodes well for Pokopia 's future DLC and content updates as well. Bubbly Basin is just one stop in its future roadmap.
